provenance.abstraction_rationale: Selected affected API torch.compile. The report demonstrates that compiling a CPU model using indirect indexing with out-of-bounds indices produces an out-of-bound read returning NaN and large values, while the same model run eagerly raises IndexError. The pattern is normalized from the issue body and comment evidence discussing missing C++ validation for indirect indexing.
unresolved_information: No explicit root-cause claim was mapped in reported_diagnosis.root_cause_claims; the mechanism is normalized from a comment describing illegal memory access during indexing and missing C++ validation.
Fix disposition is ambiguous: one comment states the issue is fixed in master via PR 98590, while another clarifies it was fixed only for CUDA at that time; the report resolution status is unknown.

historical_conditions.statement: The reported invocation compiles the model with torch.compile and executes it on CPU.

The model forward computes torch.sum(x[self.idx], dim=1), where self.idx is torch.tensor([[1, 3, 2], [1, 4, 3]]) and x has first dimension size 2, so indices 3 and 4 are out of bounds for dimension 0.
The reported environment uses PyTorch 2.1.0.dev20230419+cu118, Python 3.9.16, Ubuntu 22.04, and the model is moved to CPU.

defect_mechanism.description: torch.compile-generated C++ code for indirect indexing x[idx] does not perform runtime bounds validation for index values that are unknown until the generated C++ executes, so invalid indices cause an out-of-bound read instead of an eager-style IndexError.

observed_failure.description: Under torch.compile on CPU, torch.sum(x[self.idx], dim=1) with invalid indices completes and returns a tensor containing NaN and large out-of-bound values such as -1.7412e+38 instead of raising an IndexError.

historical_observations.statement: Running the same model without torch.compile raises IndexError: index 3 is out of bounds for dimension 0 with size 2.
A maintainer comment states the issue is fixed in master via PR 98590; a subsequent comment clarifies the fix is currently only for CUDA.
